# Results — Study 960 (The Unstaked ETF) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). We measure the realised
annualised **tracking difference** of the two US spot-Ethereum lines with a usable
history — **ETHA** (iShares) and **ETHE** (Grayscale) — against the coin (**ETH-USD**)
and against each other, then add the two declared non-tape ASSUMPTIONS (the sponsor fee
and the forgone staking yield) into a wrapper-cost ledger. Daily closes via `yfinance`
(`auto_adjust=True`). ETF-era window **2024-07-23 → 2026-06-30** — the day the US spot
ETH funds began trading, to the last complete month. As-of **2026-06-30**.*

**Labels, because they carry the argument.** ETHA and ETHE distribute nothing, so their
adjusted close is both price and **total return** of the wrapper. **ETH-USD is
price-only** — and, decisively, it is the price of an **unstaked** coin: it contains no
consensus reward. **BIL** is a genuine total return and is the cash leg of the
excess-of-cash race. **PROXY / ASSUMPTION:** the sponsor fees (ETHA 0.25%/yr, ETHE
2.50%/yr) and the net staking yield (central case 3.0%/yr) are documented external
constants, *not* measured here; both are swept below.

**Survivorship, and the coverage caveat that matters more.** No selection on outcome:
the fee ranking used here was published before the funds opened and was never re-ranked
after seeing a result, and both lines have traded continuously since day one. But the
US spot-ETH cohort that launched together on 2024-07-23 has roughly **nine** members, and
this study measures **two** of them — the two carried in the desk-wide cache. They are
also the cohort's **fee extremes**: the cheapest tier (ETHA) against the dearest line by a
wide margin (ETHE). **FETH, ETHW, ETHV, QETH, EZET and CETH are not measured here.** So the
2.25 %/yr documented gap and the 1.64 %/yr measured spread are the cohort's *upper bound*,
not a typical fund-to-fund number, and the cross-sectional replication that Study 959 runs
across ten bitcoin wrappers is **absent** from this ETH tape. The sample is in addition a
*single* 23-month episode of a single asset, which is the binding constraint on everything
that follows.

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n sessions | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ETHA, ETHE, ETH-USD, BIL | 2024-07-23 → 2026-06-30 | 486 | Fingerprint `4e34c697361e` |

## 1. The question as asked — fund vs coin

| Fund | Tracking difference (log) | Simple-return diff | 95% block-bootstrap CI (block 21) | monthly *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ETHA** vs ETH-USD | **+0.27 %/yr** | −0.31 %/yr | **[−8.86, +9.34]** | +0.11 | +0.03 |
| **ETHE** vs ETH-USD | **−1.37 %/yr** | −1.31 %/yr | **[−10.53, +7.77]** | −0.56 | −0.16 |

Both point estimates are statistically indistinguishable from zero, from each other, and
from any staking-sized number. The reason is in the second moment: the daily fund-minus-coin
difference has a standard deviation of **190 bps a day** with a lag-1 autocorrelation of
**−0.56**. The coin prints 24/7 and its daily bar is stamped several hours after the 16:00
fund close, so every session carries a large observation error that reverses the next day.

### The resolution limit is ruler-dependent — so here is the whole sweep

An earlier draft of this study quoted a single number, "±9.1 %/yr", and called it *the*
resolution limit. It is not: it is the half-width at one block length, and on a
mean-reverting difference the half-width falls as the block grows (the reversal telescopes
inside a longer block). Publishing only the middle of that range would have been a choice
dressed as a fact, so the sweep is published instead.

| Ruler (ETHA vs the coin) | b = 5 | b = 10 | **b = 21** | b = 42 | b = 63 | non-overlapping monthly |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Resolution limit at \|*t*\| = 2 | ±18.0 | ±13.2 | **±9.1** | ±6.1 | ±5.4 | **±5.0 %/yr** |

The honest statement is therefore: **the limit is between ±5.0 and ±18.0 %/yr depending on
which ruler you hold, and every one of them is larger than the ~3 %/yr effect under
discussion** — by 1.7× on the friendliest reading and 6× on the harshest. The claim
survives at every block length, which is the only reason it is allowed to stand; the tidy
"three times the effect" of the first draft was an artefact of stopping at b = 21. ETHE
against the coin sweeps the same way (±4.8 to ±17.8 %/yr). This tape could not distinguish a
3 %-a-year drag from zero if it were staring at one.

## 2. What the same estimator *can* resolve — fund vs fund

Point the identical machinery at two wrappers on the same coin, both stamped at the same
16:00 close, and the timing error cancels exactly. Daily noise collapses from 190 bps to
**11 bps**.

| Pair | Tracking difference (log) | 95% CI (block 21) | monthly *t* | iid *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ETHE − ETHA** | **−1.64 %/yr** | **[−2.27, −0.97]** | **−5.16** | −1.32 | −2.89 |

The documented sponsor-fee spread (2.50% − 0.25% = **2.25 %/yr**) sits just inside the
interval's lower edge, so the measured **1.64 %/yr** — **73%** of the documented spread — is
statistically consistent with the funds charging exactly what they say. *This is the study's
only robust real-tape number, and it is a fee measurement, not a staking measurement.*

**Which *t* are we quoting, and is it the flattering one?** Yes, and we say so. The three
rulers disagree by a factor of four and they are not equally defensible:

- **i.i.d. daily *t* = −1.32.** The widest, and it does *not* clear \|*t*\| = 2. It is the
  reading a sceptic should demand an answer to — so here it is: the daily difference of two
  closes on the same asset has a lag-1 autocorrelation of **−0.47**, essentially an MA(1)
  reversal from premium/discount noise. The variance of its *k*-day sum therefore grows far
  more slowly than *k*, and the i.i.d. daily *t* assumes that mechanical feature away. It is
  over-wide, not "safe".
- **HAC *t* = −2.89.** With a negative autocovariance the HAC variance falls *below* the
  i.i.d. one, so HAC is the **flattering** direction here, not a conservative correction.
- **Non-overlapping monthly *t* = −5.16** (24 calendar-month sums; no kernel, no block, no
  overlap) **and the block bootstrap.** These are what the verdict is read from.

Three checks decide whether that choice is doing the work: **22 of 24 months are negative**;
**jackknifing a whole month out** at a time moves the estimate only between −1.79 and
−1.51 %/yr; and the interval **excludes zero at every block length** (half-widths 1.15 / 0.84
/ 0.65 / 0.61 / 0.59 %/yr at b = 5/10/21/42/63, monthly ±0.62). Unlike the fund-vs-coin leg,
this one does not depend on which ruler you pick.

**Do not read the simple-return column as the holder's benefit.** ETHE − ETHA reads
−1.64 %/yr on the log measure and −1.00 %/yr as a difference of annualised *simple* returns.
The two describe the same fact — the ETHE/ETHA ratio fell **3.1%** over 1.92 years — and the
log figure is the compounding-correct one, i.e. what a holder who switched actually kept.
The simple-return difference is level-dependent and shrinks on an asset that halved.

## 3. The wrapper-cost ledger — where the staking yield actually enters

ETH-USD is the price of an **unstaked** coin. The forgone consensus reward is therefore
**absent by construction** from every number in section 1: it is not a small effect buried
in noise, it is an effect the benchmark cannot contain. It enters only as an addition
relative to a hypothetical **self-staking** coin holder.

| Fund | Measured TD vs the (unstaked) coin | ASSUMED fee | ASSUMED staking | Shortfall vs a self-staking holder | Staking share of declared cost |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ETHA** | +0.27 %/yr | 0.25 % | 3.00 % | **−2.73 %/yr** | **92 %** |
| **ETHE** | −1.37 %/yr | 2.50 % | 3.00 % | **−4.37 %/yr** | **55 %** |

Read the last column carefully: it is arithmetic on two constants, and the tape
contributes nothing to it. The honest one-line answer to *"what share of the gap does
staking account for?"* is: **on the cheap wrapper, essentially all of the declared cost —
but the declared cost was declared, not observed.**

The residual the tape *does* speak to — measured TD minus the fee we expected — is
**+0.52 %/yr** (ETHA) and **+1.13 %/yr** (ETHE): both funds slightly *out*-tracked their own
posted fee. Both residuals sit far inside even the **narrowest** resolution limit (±5.0 and
±4.8 %/yr on the non-overlapping monthly ruler, never mind ±9 at block 21), so the correct
reading is "no evidence of anything", not "the funds beat their fees".

## 4. Assumption sweeps (the staking yield is not tape, so it is never asserted)

| ASSUMED net staking yield | ETHA shortfall vs a staking holder | Staking share |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2.0 %/yr | −1.73 %/yr | 89 % |
| 2.5 %/yr | −2.23 %/yr | 91 % |
| **3.0 %/yr (central)** | **−2.73 %/yr** | **92 %** |
| 3.5 %/yr | −3.23 %/yr | 93 % |
| 4.5 %/yr | −4.23 %/yr | 95 % |

Sweeping ETHA's effective sponsor fee across its waiver range (0.12% → 0.25%) moves the
staking share from 96% to 92%. The conclusion is insensitive to both assumptions, because
the assumptions are the *only* inputs — which is precisely the criticism.

## 5. Era cut (split 2025-07-01)

A cost that is a *fee* is flat across eras; a cost that is a forgone *staking* yield
collapses the moment a fund starts staking. That makes the era cut the only tape-side
handle on the staking hypothesis — and it is a weak one, with ~250 sessions a side.

| Pair | Era | n | TD | 95% CI | monthly *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ETHA vs coin | 2024-07 → 2025-06 | 235 | +0.36 %/yr | [−13.50, +15.69] | +0.08 |
| ETHA vs coin | 2025-07 → 2026-06 | 250 | +0.19 %/yr | [−10.73, +11.67] | +0.06 |
| ETHE vs coin | 2024-07 → 2025-06 | 235 | −2.07 %/yr | [−16.08, +13.16] | −0.46 |
| ETHE vs coin | 2025-07 → 2026-06 | 250 | −0.71 %/yr | [−11.52, +10.75] | −0.25 |
| **ETHE − ETHA** | 2024-07 → 2025-06 | 235 | **−2.43 %/yr** | [−3.51, −1.39] | −6.25 |
| **ETHE − ETHA** | 2025-07 → 2026-06 | 250 | **−0.90 %/yr** | [−1.72, −0.02] | −2.02 |

The fund-vs-coin rows are uninformative in both halves (intervals ±11 to ±16 %/yr). The
fund-vs-fund spread, however, **narrows by 1.5 pp** between the halves, and the calendar
table below shows the same shape: −2.14 %/yr (2024), −1.97 %/yr (2025), −0.52 %/yr (2026,
123 sessions). Something changed in the relative economics of the two wrappers during the
sample — a fee change, a waiver rolling off, or one fund beginning to stake would all
produce this. **This tape cannot tell you which**, and we do not pretend otherwise.

## 6. Is the measured spread bankable? Long ETHA / short ETHE

Dollar-neutral, one unit a side, weights formed from the two published fees through day
*t* and held from *t+1* (**the study's single execution lag**), 10 bps one-way × NAV on each
leg in and out, and an explicit annual borrow on the short leg. The book is dollar-neutral,
so short proceeds fund the long leg and **no cash rebate is credited** anywhere. Gross
**+1.85 %/yr** at 1.72% annualised vol, on the same three rulers as section 2: **monthly
*t* = +5.69 with 21 of 24 months positive** (the reading quoted), HAC *t* = +3.32 (the
flattering direction), i.i.d. daily *t* = +1.50 (the over-wide bound, which does not clear 2).

| Short-leg borrow | Net | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/yr (general collateral fantasy) | +1.45 %/yr | −0.47 % |
| 50 bps/yr | +0.95 %/yr | −0.51 % |
| 100 bps/yr | +0.45 %/yr | −0.56 % |
| **200 bps/yr** | **−0.55 %/yr** | −1.08 % |
| 400 bps/yr | −2.55 %/yr | −4.17 % |
| 800 bps/yr | −6.55 %/yr | −11.23 % |

Break-even borrow is about **145 bps/yr**. A Grayscale-style crypto trust is not a
general-collateral name, and the spread itself has been shrinking (section 5), so the
arbitrage expression of this finding is not something to rely on. The *un*-levered version
— simply owning the cheaper wrapper — keeps the whole spread with no borrow and one trade.

## 7. Excess-of-cash race (both arms minus BIL)

Reported for completeness and read with a straight face: the two arms hold the same coin,
so the race can only ever surface the drag, and a 72%-vol asset over two years cannot.

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | Advantage vs coin | HAC *t* | i.i.d. *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ETHA (net of a 5 bps entry) | −0.260 | +0.038 | +0.24 | +0.10 |
| ETHE (net of a 5 bps entry) | −0.290 | +0.009 | +0.01 | +0.00 |
| ETH-USD (coin, price-only) | −0.299 | — | — | — |

All three arms are excess of BIL's total return. Every Sharpe is negative — the ETF era so
far has been a bear market in ETH — and the differences are noise.

## 8. Synthetic control (machinery proof; never supports the stamp)

One coin, a mis-timed vendor close, and two wrappers separated by a **planted 2.25 %/yr**
drag spread:

- fund-vs-fund estimate **−2.24 %/yr**, CI [−3.05, −1.45], monthly *t* = −5.84 — the planted
  truth recovered to within 0.01 pp, interval clear of zero;
- fund-vs-coin estimate on the *same world*: **+0.28 %/yr**, CI [−12.01, +12.95] — a
  resolution limit **16× wider** than the fund-vs-fund one, and five times the size of the
  effect it is supposed to find;
- null (identical wrappers, 8 seeds): fund-vs-fund mean **−0.011 %/yr** (sd 0.065), fires on
  **0/8**.

The detector recovers a planted effect and stays quiet on the null. The real-tape silence
in section 1 is therefore a property of *the benchmark and the sample*, not of a broken
harness — which is exactly the claim this study makes.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** Two legs, two answers. The leg the question asked about is **absent**:
  the realised fund-vs-coin tracking difference is **+0.27 %/yr** (ETHA) with a
  bootstrap interval of **[−8.9, +9.3]** and a monthly *t* of **+0.11**, so this tape cannot
  see a staking-sized drag — and more fundamentally *cannot ever*, because ETH-USD is itself
  the price of an unstaked coin, from which the forgone reward is missing by construction.
  The leg the tape *can* see is **real**: the ETHE−ETHA spread is **−1.64 %/yr** with a
  bootstrap CI of **[−2.27, −0.97]** and a monthly *t* of **−5.16**, and it recovers 73% of a
  documented 2.25%/yr fee gap that sits inside the interval. So: a real, robust measurement
  of the *fee*, and nothing at all on the *staking*, whose 92%-of-declared-cost share is
  arithmetic on two external constants rather than a finding.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** There is a genuine, bankable action here — own the cheap
  wrapper, not the dear one, worth the **measured 1.64 %/yr** (a 3.1% terminal-wealth
  difference over 1.92 years) against a **documented** 2.25 %/yr fee gap; the measurement,
  not the fee schedule, is what the tape supports. But it
  rests on 23 months of one asset **and on the cohort's two fee extremes — six other spot-ETH
  lines are not measured here**, so this is the widest available pair, not a typical one. The
  spread has already narrowed from −2.43 %/yr to
  −0.90 %/yr, and the levered expression (long ETHA / short ETHE) dies above ~145 bps of
  borrow. The larger prize — the ~3 %/yr staking yield — cannot be banked from inside any
  wrapper tested here; capturing it means leaving the ETF entirely for self-custody or a
  staking provider, taking on lock-up, slashing, counterparty and tax treatment that this
  tape says nothing about.
- **The methodological point, which outlasts the numbers.** Before quoting anyone a
  tracking difference against a 24/7 asset, compute the interval — **and then compute it
  again on a different ruler.** Here it lands between **±5.0 and ±18.0 %/yr** depending on the
  block length, and the single tidy "±9" of the first draft was the middle of that range
  presented as a fact. Every ruler is still larger than the ~3 %/yr effect, which is why the
  conclusion holds; had the sweep straddled 3 %/yr the honest verdict would have been "we
  don't know", not "it isn't there". The same estimator against a *same-close* benchmark
  resolves 1.64 %/yr with a monthly *t* of −5.16 and an interval that excludes zero at every
  block length. The benchmark, not the estimator, decides whether the question is answerable.
